headline: Volume has ramped nearly 60% over the prior block while easy-run HR sits meaningfully lower on comparable efforts.
confidence_reasons: Multiple data sources active in last 3 days
summary:
The story remains the aerobic response to your volume increase, but the angle worth naming today is the durability of that response as the load keeps stacking. You've held a steadily rising block without easy-effort HR creeping back up — the drift is going the other way. That combination, more kilometres at lower cardiac cost, is the clearest signal that the base is genuinely absorbing the ramp rather than just tolerating it.

What's less settled is whether that HR gain has yet converted into faster paces at the same effort. So far the evidence is a cleaner heart rate, not obviously quicker easy running — a distinction worth staying honest about before calling it an economy gain outright.

Strength volume has ticked down slightly against the prior block. Not a concern in isolation, but with running load elevated it's the balancing item to keep honest, especially given the loaded-pack demands of the trail crossing next month.
watch_items: Watch whether easy pace at the same low HR starts drifting quicker — that would firm the economy interpretation beyond the HR drop alone.
Note how longer and back-to-back efforts sit under a loaded pack, since that specific demand still isn't reflected in recent runs.
Keep strength frequency from sliding further as running volume stays high through the pre-event weeks.
Zone 2 minutes are sitting below the weekly floor while grey-zone time is near zero — worth watching that easy volume doesn't get squeezed as total load rises.

evidence_items.text: ▲ 4-week volume 146 km vs 92 km prior block (+59%)
▼ Easy-run HR averaging 143 bpm vs 155 bpm prior period (comparable-effort runs, 7 vs 6 runs)
